subject: MAP: Performance validation plan — hosted / dedicated / private stability tests
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP: Performance validation plan — hosted / dedicated / private stability tests

Jordan — thanks for the call today. As discussed, attaching a concise MAP-style validation plan to operationalize the performance evals across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. High-level asks below; full checklist in attachment (MAP_PerfPlan_NovaHealth_v1.pdf).

Quick plan (weeks 1–2):
- Scope: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and stability under target concurrency (100, 300, 1k) and background load.
- Environments: Redwood Hosted (us-west), Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool), Nova Private (VPC/on-prem staging).
- Test harness: load-gen-2000 (locally-managed), synthetic and replay prompts from Nova sample corpus (200k tokens).
- Success criteria: p95 latency within SLA band per environment; <5% throughput variance across 30-min steady-state windows; no KV-cache regressions.

Immediate asks from Nova:
1) Confirm dates for runs (we suggested 9/15–9/17).
2) Provide sample prompt set and a representative concurrency distribution (spike vs steady).
3) Share any additional SSO/KMS access prerequisites for Private tests.

Attachments: MAP_PerfPlan_NovaHealth_v1.pdf (checklists + runbook), sample prompt manifest referenced inside.

Next step: if you confirm the prompt set and dates we’ll schedule dedicated test windows and share runbook with engineering.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Jordan / Evelyn — tagging engineering details and runbook notes. We’ll run smoke tests on Hosted and Private Thursday (9/15) morning to validate setup; full runs on 9/16. Key test specifics:
- Measurement windows: 30s warmup, 30m steady-state, 5–10m burst windows for each concurrency point.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, TTFT, worker queue lag, GPU util, autoscale events (scale-up time, scaled pods), and KV cache hit ratio.
- Load generation: load-gen-2000 with per-session prefix caching enabled to simulate production patterns; we’ll also run a pure synthetic (no cache) loop to quantify cache benefit.
- Background job: run a low-priority batch that saturates disk I/O on the Private host to observe noisy-neighbor effects.

We will upload the perf-runbook.md to the shared Drive and post links before Thursday. If SRE from Nova can provision the SSH user and KMS policies by EOD tomorrow we’re good to go.

-Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@novahealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-17T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation plan — hosted / dedicated / private stability tests

Jordan — sharing the consolidated results from the 9/16 runs (attached: results_20270916.csv, graphs_20270916.zip). Summary highlights:

Hosted (Redwood managed, us-west) — baseline
- Concurrency tested: 100 / 300 / 1000 sessions.
- p50: 48ms (100c) / 64ms (300c) / 120ms (1k)
- p95: 220ms / 310ms / 520ms
- p99: 480ms / 820ms / 1400ms
- TTFT: 35ms median
- Throughput (tokens/sec): 3.2k (100c steady) -> 18.5k (1k burst)
- Notes: Hosted autoscale triggered on the 1k burst at ~28s; tail latency spike observed during scale-up window but smoothed after 90s.

Dedicated (reserved pool, same region) — predictable
- p50: 34ms / 50ms / 88ms
- p95: 120ms / 180ms / 320ms
- p99: 260ms / 420ms / 640ms
- TTFT: 28ms median
- Throughput: 4.1k (100c) -> 21.7k (1k)
- Notes: Dedicated showed the lowest tail latency and fastest recovery; no autoscale-induced spike since capacity was pre-warmed.

Private (Nova staging VPC) — variable depending on isolation
- p50: 36ms / 58ms / 95ms
- p95: 150ms / 260ms / 520ms
- p99: 310ms / 680ms / 1200ms
- TTFT: 30ms median
- Throughput: 3.8k -> 19.0k
- Notes: With the background batch (disk-heavy) running we observed 8–12% throughput variance and occasional GC pauses on the on-prem host; predictability improved when we moved batch to a separate I/O tier.

Key takeaways for Nova:
- Dedicated provides the most predictable 95/99 tail behavior and fastest TTFT under sustained high concurrency — best fit if strict SLAs are critical.
- Hosted is cost-efficient and handled peak traffic with short-lived tail spikes during autoscale; recommend tuned warm pools for tight tail targets.
- Private works well but requires SRE-level isolation (separate I/O nodes / network shaping) to match Dedicated-level predictability.

Action items we recommend:
1) For a production launch with strict latency SLAs, proceed with a Dedicated commitment and a 30–90 day prewarm window.
2) If Private is preferred for data residency, add an I/O isolation plan and a scheduled prewarming policy.
3) Redwood can provide a 90-day Dedicated trial addendum; see attached addendum-dedicated-trial.docx for commercial terms.

Let us know if you want a short walk-through of the CSV/graphs on 9/18.

—Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance validation plan — hosted / dedicated / private stability tests

Jordan / Amir — thanks for the quick turnaround and for provisioning access. Based on the results, Nova Health has two pragmatic options:

Option A (recommended): Move forward with Dedicated capacity for production cutover. Redwood will:
- Provide a 90-day Dedicated trial (no commit up-front) so you can validate production traffic patterns.
- Prewarm capacity + set a warm pool config to avoid autoscale tail spikes.
- Deliver an isolation checklist for Private if you later wish to migrate on-prem.

Option B: Use Hosted with aggressive warm-pool and autoscale tuning; lower cost but expect brief tail spikes on unanticipated bursts.

Proposed close timeline (high level):
- 9/20: Legal receives proposed addendum (we’ll send DocuSign).
- 9/24: Commercial sign-off; ingest PO / billing details.
- 10/01: Dedicated trial capacity available; kickoff runbook + SRE onboarding.

Next steps from our side: attach addendum-dedicated-trial.docx and DocuSign link in the HubSpot deal. Jordan — if that timeline looks OK I’ll route the DocuSign to Amir for review and signature.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 20m call if you want to walk the graphs with Marcus and Rishi.

Best,
